decisions.label: Rendered-HTML Markdown corpus (not wikitext)
decisions.detail: Fetched Wikipedia's rendered HTML (the same content a browser shows, via the /api/rest_v1/page/html/ endpoint) and converted to Markdown with markdownify/BeautifulSoup, stripping only script/style/meta tags. Keeps infobox tables, citation footnotes, navboxes, and category links (absolutized to full URLs) that v2's wikitext parser deliberately dropped as clutter. 3.6-8.2x more faithful units per language than v2's corpus as a result.

decisions.label: Same 4 languages as v1/v2
decisions.detail: English, Hindi, Telugu, Marathi — this version changes the corpus-building method, not the language set.

decisions.label: Same core pipeline as v2
decisions.detail: Metaspace pre-tokenizer + decoder, NFKC-only normalizer, explicit [UNK] token, BPE model, 10,000-token budget — unchanged from v2. Only the corpus differs.

decisions.label: Same 3-group merge strategy
decisions.detail: English alone, Telugu alone, Hindi+Marathi trained jointly (they share Devanagari) — same reasoning as v1/v2.

decisions.label: Symmetric equalization across all 3 groups
decisions.detail: Same allocation-search strategy as v2: binary search for the smallest common fertility target that all three groups can reach within the 10,000-token budget, no group privileged.

decisions.label: Hindi:Marathi joint-training weight re-tuned
decisions.detail: 3:7 here vs v2's 2:3 — the richer corpus grew Hindi's size relative to Marathi's (from ~1.8x to ~3.0x), so Marathi needs more counter-weight to balance against Hindi's larger frequency pool.

cons.label: OOV characters still break exact round-trip
cons.detail: Same as v2 — an unrecognized character decodes back as the literal string "[UNK]", not the original character.

cons.label: Larger vocab dedup during merging
cons.detail: This corpus's 3 groups share more vocabulary (common URLs, digits, Latin acronyms) than v2's did, so more of the allocated 10,000-token budget gets deduplicated away during the merge step (final vocab 8,503 vs the 10,000 allocated) — leaving less precision in the equalization than the pre-merge search predicted.

cons.label: Slightly worse spread than v2, despite the richer corpus
cons.detail: Score ≈10,388 here vs v2's ≈16,581 — the bigger corpus gets fertility down to the assignment solution's own reported range (0.69-0.79 vs v2's 1.15-1.21), but doesn't automatically mean a tighter spread across languages, partly due to the dedup effect above.
